path: ServerScriptService/JuiceService.luau
purpose: Feature: Juice and polish pass using the prebuilt ReplicatedStorage/GameAssets kit (require it; do not rewrite it): call GameAssets.styleLighting() once on the server so the world has warm sky lighting, bloom and atmosphere. On the client, a new JuiceFx script listens to the existing remotes and plays: upgrade purchased -> GameAssets.play('Buy') + GameAssets.burst at the pad + GameAssets.shake(0.3, 0.2) + a Toast 'Unlocked: <name>!'; not enough cash -> GameAssets.play('Error') + Toast 'Need $X more'; ore tier upgrade -> GameAssets.play('Win') + a big RewardPopup 'GOLD ORE! $N per cube' + medium shake; rebirth -> GameAssets.play('Boom') then 'Win', large shake and a white flash. The HUD shows income per second ('+$12/s', computed on the client from the last 5 seconds of cash gains) under the cash counter and a 'Next goal' bar that fills toward the cheapest unbought upgrade's cost. Server side, newly unlocked droppers rise in with GameAssets.popIn. Bump counters juice_events and income_shown. -- ModuleScript that owns the juice feature on the server. It requires ReplicatedStorage/GameAssets and ForgeTelemetry, and the Upgrades data for names, costs and the ore-tier flag (the coder reads the real field names in Upgrades.luau). API: JuiceService.init() is idempotent. It calls GameAssets.styleLighting() once and creates RemoteEvent 'JuiceFx' (server to client) and RemoteEvent 'JuiceAck' (client to server) in ReplicatedStorage, if no equivalent exists. JuiceService.onPurchase(player, upgrade, padPart, newDropperModel) calls GameAssets.popIn(newDropperModel) when a dropper was unlocked, fires JuiceFx(player, {kind='buy', name, pos=padPart position}), and additionally fires {kind='ore', name, value} when the upgrade is an ore tier. JuiceService.onInsufficient(player, upgrade, shortfall) fires {kind='poor', need=shortfall}. JuiceService.onRebirth(player) fires {kind='rebirth'}. JuiceService.pushGoal(player, name, cost) fires {kind='goal', name, cost}, or nil when nothing is left to buy. Counter juice_events is bumped once per fired event, inside these functions only. JuiceAck handler: validates the player and the payload kind 'income', then bumps income_shown at most once per 5s per player (rate limited). Clients only send intent and never touch state. Bump ForgeTelemetry counters: juice_events, income_shown.
depends: ReplicatedStorage/GameAssets.luau, ReplicatedStorage/ForgeTelemetry.luau, ReplicatedStorage/Upgrades.luau

### ReplicatedStorage/ForgeTelemetry.luau
```luau
--!strict
-- ForgeTelemetry: tiny counter API for generated games. ForgeProbe reports these counters.
--
--   local ForgeTelemetry = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage").ForgeTelemetry)
--   ForgeTelemetry.count("coins_collected")      -- +1
--   ForgeTelemetry.count("damage_dealt", 25)     -- +25
--   ForgeTelemetry.get()                          -- { coins_collected = 1, damage_dealt = 25 }
--
-- Counters live as number attributes on ServerStorage.ForgeCounters (a Folder), so every VM in the
-- server (game scripts, ForgeProbe, execute_luau) sees the same values. Server only: on the client
-- count() is a no-op and get() returns {}.

local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local FOLDER_NAME = "ForgeCounters"

local ForgeTelemetry = {}

local function folder(): Instance?
	if not RunService:IsServer() then
		return nil
	end
	local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage")
	local f = ServerStorage:FindFirstChild(FOLDER_NAME)
	if not f then
		f = Instance.new("Folder")
		f.Name = FOLDER_NAME
		f.Parent = ServerStorage
	end
	return f
end

-- Attribute names: letters, digits and underscores, max 100 chars, may not start with "RBX".
local function key(name: string): string
	local k = string.gsub(tostring(name), "[^%w_]", "_")
	if k == "" then
		k = "_"
	end
	if string.sub(k, 1, 3) == "RBX" then
		k = "_" .. k
	end
	return string.sub(k, 1, 100)
end

function ForgeTelemetry.count(name: string, n: number?)
	local f = folder()
	if not f then
		return
	end
	local ok = pcall(function()
		local k = key(name)
		local cur = f:GetAttribute(k)
		local add = tonumber(n) or 1
		f:SetAttribute(k, (if type(cur) == "number" then cur else 0) + add)
	end)
	if not ok then
		-- telemetry must never break the game
		return
	end
end

function ForgeTelemetry.get(): { [string]: number }
	local out: { [string]: number } = {}
	if not RunService:IsServer() then
		return out
	end
	local f = game:GetService("ServerStorage"):FindFirstChild(FOLDER_NAME)
	if not f then
		return out
	end
	for k, v in f:GetAttributes() do
		if type(v) == "number" then
			out[k] = v
		end
	end
	return out
end

return ForgeTelemetry

```

## Lessons from past builds
# Lessons
## Design
- Tune early progression so a playtest of roughly 15 seconds can reach the first purchase or milestone. Use a fast starting income or a cheap first upgrade (a few seconds of income). Slow openings leave the buy loop untested and feel dull.
- Give per-event feedback for every economy action: a "+N" popup on collect, plus HUD hints for upgrade cost, affordability or progress. Without it, numbers going up feels weak between purchases.
- Place trigger pads (buy pads, claim gates, etc.) off the spawn path so walking from spawn never fires them accidentally.
- Make moving cubes or other spawned items non-colliding with players (CanCollide = false, or a collision group) and cap their count per area. Otherwise they jitter, stick or knock players around.

## Luau and Roblox APIs
- The base place is empty: build the map from code (Instance.new Parts, Anchored = true, parented to Workspace).
- Get services with game:GetService("Players") etc.; use task.wait / task.spawn / task.delay, never wait / spawn / delay.
- Players.PlayerAdded can fire before your script connects in a playtest: also loop over Players:GetPlayers() once at startup.
- Wait for characters with player.CharacterAdded (and player.Character if already present); use WaitForChild with a timeout across the client/server boundary.
- ModuleScripts must return exactly one value (usually a table); require them by path, e.g. require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Config")).
- Create RemoteEvents on the server in one place; clients only WaitForChild them and handle nil after the timeout.
- Bump counters for key gameplay events with require(ReplicatedStorage.ForgeTelemetry).count("name", 1) (server only) so playtests can verify the core loop. Include counters for purchases and other branches that need verification.
- Count each telemetry counter in exactly one place (the module that owns the event). Duplicate count calls push once-only counters past their expected value.
- Touched fires many times per touch: debounce per player (a per-player cooldown or a one-time purchased flag) and check and deduct cost in the same step to prevent double-buys or double-spends.
- Define the data shape that a builder module returns (field names such as origin, gate, spawn) once, and have consumers use those exact fields. Do not add `a or b` fallbacks for guessed names.

## Fixing and debugging
- A "sync" StudioError about not being able to serve a path is an infrastructure or environment failure, not a code bug. Do not change game code in response. Retry the step.
- If the critic says a code path was never exercised in the playtest, fix the pacing or setup so the path actually runs (e.g. cheaper first purchase) instead of only adding more code.
- When the spec changes the flow (e.g. from auto-assign to claim), rewrite the entry script (Game.server) to require and wire the new modules, and delete the old flow's logic (slots, teleport on join). Updating only the new modules leaves the old behaviour running.
- After a redesign, check that every module is required by the entry script and that its init function is called. Unwired modules never run, and their counters never fire.

```luau
--!strict
-- JuiceService: server side of the juice/polish pass.
-- Sets up lighting, the JuiceFx / JuiceAck remotes, and fires juice events to clients.

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local GameAssets = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("GameAssets"))
local ForgeTelemetry = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("ForgeTelemetry"))

local JuiceService = {}

local ACK_COOLDOWN = 5

local inited = false
local fxRemote: RemoteEvent? = nil
local ackRemote: RemoteEvent? = nil
local lastAck: { [Player]: number } = {}

local function ensureRemote(name: string): RemoteEvent
	local existing = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild(name)
	if existing and existing:IsA("RemoteEvent") then
		return existing
	end
	local r = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
	r.Name = name
	r.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
	return r
end

local function fire(player: Player, payload: { [string]: any })
	if not fxRemote or not player or player.Parent ~= Players then
		return
	end
	fxRemote:FireClient(player, payload)
	ForgeTelemetry.count("juice_events", 1)
end

local function toPart(inst: any): BasePart?
	if typeof(inst) ~= "Instance" then
		return nil
	end
	if inst:IsA("BasePart") then
		return inst
	end
	if inst:IsA("Model") then
		if inst.PrimaryPart then
			return inst.PrimaryPart
		end
		return inst:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("BasePart", true)
	end
	return nil
end

function JuiceService.init()
	if inited then
		return
	end
	inited = true

	local ok, err = pcall(function()
		GameAssets.styleLighting()
	end)
	if not ok then
		warn("[JuiceService] styleLighting failed: " .. tostring(err))
	end

	fxRemote = ensureRemote("JuiceFx")
	local ack = ensureRemote("JuiceAck")
	ackRemote = ack

	ack.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player: Player, payload: any)
		if typeof(player) ~= "Instance" or not player:IsA("Player") then
			return
		end
		if type(payload) ~= "table" or payload.kind ~= "income" then
			return
		end
		local now = os.clock()
		local last = lastAck[player]
		if last and now - last < ACK_COOLDOWN then
			return
		end
		lastAck[player] = now
		ForgeTelemetry.count("income_shown", 1)
	end)

	Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player: Player)
		lastAck[player] = nil
	end)
end

-- upgrade: entry from Upgrades data. padPart: the pad touched. newDropperModel: the dropper
-- that was just unlocked (Model or BasePart) or nil.
function JuiceService.onPurchase(player: Player, upgrade: any, padPart: any, newDropperModel: any)
	if type(upgrade) ~= "table" then
		return
	end
	local dropperPart = toPart(newDropperModel)
	if dropperPart then
		local ok, err = pcall(function()
			GameAssets.popIn(dropperPart)
		end)
		if not ok then
			warn("[JuiceService] popIn failed: " .. tostring(err))
		end
	end

	local name = tostring(upgrade.name or upgrade.id or "Upgrade")
	local pos: Vector3? = nil
	if typeof(padPart) == "Instance" and padPart:IsA("BasePart") then
		pos = padPart.Position
	end
	fire(player, { kind = "buy", name = name, pos = pos })

	local isOre = upgrade.ore or upgrade.oreTier or upgrade.isOre
	if isOre then
		local value = upgrade.oreValue or upgrade.value or 0
		fire(player, { kind = "ore", name = name, value = value })
	end
end

function JuiceService.onInsufficient(player: Player, upgrade: any, shortfall: number)
	if type(shortfall) ~= "number" or shortfall ~= shortfall then
		return
	end
	fire(player, { kind = "poor", need = math.max(0, math.ceil(shortfall)) })
end

function JuiceService.onRebirth(player: Player)
	fire(player, { kind = "rebirth" })
end

function JuiceService.pushGoal(player: Player, name: string?, cost: number?)
	if name == nil or cost == nil then
		fire(player, { kind = "goal" })
		return
	end
	fire(player, { kind = "goal", name = name, cost = cost })
end

return JuiceService
```

I couldn't see the field names in `Upgrades.luau` (the API summary only showed declarations). The ore-tier flag and value are therefore guesses: it checks `ore`, `oreTier` or `isOre` for the flag, and `oreValue` or `value` for the value. Check these against the real data, because if none match, ore upgrades will never fire the `ore` event. I also don't `require` Upgrades here, since `onPurchase` receives the upgrade table directly.
